_why: MOD-08, TRUST-06, TRUST-02. An ADDON LAYER's checks file, beside the synthetic-NIC layer's script triple at labs/clusters/grid-core/addons/dra-nic/checks.json — not a module checks path, so it carries no Truth Contract tag. Every entry asserts OBJECT STATE (STANDARDS.md C26): a DeviceClass and its selector, this driver's ResourceSlices and the attributes on them, a DaemonSet's ready count, the digest a running container resolved, and the committed object set. None asserts a performance number and none a Pod phase. THE DEVICES ARE SYNTHETIC NICs from a second release of the upstream example driver on its net profile: their nic-N names, model string and bandwidth capacity are constants in the driver's source and not readings, so no entry reads any of them and STANDARDS.md C15 Group 3 captions them wherever they reach a page. A synthetic NIC is never called a NIC on hardware. ONLY THIS DRIVER'S SLICES are counted, selected by spec.driver, because addon-dra's slices are on the same nodes — which is also why addon-dra's own checks file does not pass while this layer is applied (it asserts every slice is its driver's). Every kubectl run sets KUBECONFIG itself and names the context, for addon-dra's measured reason. Every entry that reads a layer file uses the dual-layout idiom (d=clusters/... || d=labs/...) from first authoring, so it resolves in a learner's clone of the public labs repository and in the source tree alike (D-08).

checks.describe: the DeviceClass sim-nic.example.com exists and its CEL selector names the same driver. The chart puts the one driverName value on the driver, the DeviceClass name and the selector together, so a DeviceClass whose selector named another driver would match no synthetic NIC and every claim against it would stay unallocated with no error on the claim

this driver's ResourceSlices, counted by spec.driver ONLY because addon-dra's slices sit on the same nodes: at least one, every one carrying the configured four synthetic NICs (kubeletPlugin.numDevices in values.yaml), and one of them on grid-core-worker, the real worker the co-allocation lab's Pod lands on. Printed as one line so zero slices, a wrong per-slice count or a slice on no real worker each fail distinguishably. The devices are SYNTHETIC NICs: their names, model string and bandwidth capacity are constants in the driver's source, which is why no entry here reads any of them
checks.run: KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core get resourceslices -o json | jq -r --arg d sim-nic.example.com '[.items[] | select(.spec.driver == $d)] as $s | "nic_slices=" + ($s | length | tostring) + " devices_per_slice=" + ([$s[].spec.devices | length] | unique | map(tostring) | join(",")) + " on_worker=" + (if ([$s[].spec.nodeName] | index("grid-core-worker")) != null then "yes" else "no" end)'

checks.describe: every synthetic NIC this driver publishes carries a non-empty resource.kubernetes.io/pcieRoot attribute, printed as with/total with a backreference so zero synthetic NICs cannot pass. values.yaml sets netPublishPCIeRoot: true because the chart default is false, and without the attribute a matchAttribute claim across the two drivers has nothing to match on
checks.run: KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core get resourceslices -o json | jq -r --arg d sim-nic.example.com --arg k resource.kubernetes.io/pcieRoot '[.items[] | select(.spec.driver == $d) | .spec.devices[]] as $n | "pcieroot=" + ([$n[] | .attributes[$k].string | select(. != null and . != "")] | length | tostring) + "/" + ($n | length | tostring)'

checks.describe: THE PROPERTY M6's CO-ALLOCATION RESTS ON, as object state: on every node this driver publishes on, each PCIe root a synthetic NIC carries is also carried by at least one of addon-dra's sim-accelerator.example.com synthetic devices on that same node. Printed with the synthetic-NIC count so an empty set cannot pass. This is what makes a claim with matchAttribute on resource.kubernetes.io/pcieRoot satisfiable; which pair the scheduler then picks is its choice and is not asserted here
checks.run: KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core get resourceslices -o json | jq -r --arg nic sim-nic.example.com --arg acc sim-accelerator.example.com --arg k resource.kubernetes.io/pcieRoot 'def roots($d; $n): [.items[] | select(.spec.driver == $d and .spec.nodeName == $n) | .spec.devices[].attributes[$k].string | select(. != null)] | unique; . as $all | ([.items[] | select(.spec.driver == $nic) | .spec.devices[]] | length) as $count | ([.items[] | select(.spec.driver == $nic) | .spec.nodeName] | unique | map(. as $n | ($all | roots($nic; $n)) - ($all | roots($acc; $n)) | length) | add // 0) as $u | "nic_devices=" + ($count | tostring) + " unshared_roots=" + ($u | tostring)'

checks.describe: the synthetic-NIC kubelet plugin DaemonSet in its own namespace reports numberReady equal to desiredNumberScheduled, and non-zero. Ready is the DaemonSet controller's count of Ready pods, not a Pod phase, and 0 of 0 is an un-applied layer rather than a pass
checks.run: KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n dra-example-driver-nic get ds dra-example-driver-nic-kubeletplugin -o json | jq -r '"plugin desired=" + (.status.desiredNumberScheduled | tostring) + " ready=" + (.status.numberReady | tostring)'

checks.describe: the imageID every Running synthetic-NIC plugin container resolved carries the index digest the committed rendered-pinned.yaml names — read from that file, so this entry and the object set cannot disagree — folded as pinned/total with a backreference so zero running containers cannot pass. The render proves what was asked for; this proves what ran
checks.run: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && d=clusters/grid-core/addons/dra-nic && { [ -d "$d" ] || d=labs/$d; } && DIG=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*image:[[:space:]]*[^@]*@\(sha256:[0-9a-f]\{64\}\).*$/\1/p' "$d/rendered-pinned.yaml" | sort -u | tr -d '\n') && KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG:-/tmp/grid-core.kubeconfig}" kubectl --context kind-grid-core -n dra-example-driver-nic get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=dra-example-driver-nic,app.kubernetes.io/component=kubeletplugin --field-selector status.phase=Running -o json | jq -r --arg dig "$DIG" '[.items[].status.containerStatuses[]?.imageID] | "plugin_containers_pinned=" + ([.[] | select($dig != "" and contains($dig))] | length | tostring) + "/" + (length | tostring)'

checks.describe: PLAT-01 over this layer's own committed artifact, needing no cluster: every image: line in rendered-pinned.yaml carries an @sha256 digest, counted as references and unpinned so an empty or truncated render cannot satisfy it
checks.run: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && d=clusters/grid-core/addons/dra-nic && { [ -d "$d" ] || d=labs/$d; } && sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*image:[[:space:]]*\(.*\)$/\1/p' "$d/rendered-pinned.yaml" | awk 'BEGIN{n=0;bad=0}{n++; if (index($0,"@sha256:")==0) bad++}END{printf "image_refs=%d unpinned=%d\n", n, bad}'

checks.describe: D-50 over the two committed artifacts, needing no cluster: this layer's rendered-pinned.yaml names the same chart commit in its header and the same single image digest as addon-dra's rendered-pinned.yaml beside it. A second release of the driver built from a different commit or image would be a second driver build passed off as the same one, and the co-allocation lab would then be comparing two different drivers. Both commits and both digest sets are compared and counted, so a missing header or an image-less file fails
checks.run: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && d=clusters/grid-core/addons/dra-nic && { [ -d "$d" ] || d=labs/$d; } && c() { sed -n 's/^# at git tag [^ ]* (commit \([0-9a-f]\{40\}\)).*$/\1/p' "$1" | head -1; } && g() { sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*image:[[:space:]]*[^@]*@\(sha256:[0-9a-f]\{64\}\).*$/\1/p' "$1" | sort -u | tr '\n' ' '; } && N="$d/rendered-pinned.yaml" && A="$d/../dra/rendered-pinned.yaml" && cn=$(c "$N") && ca=$(c "$A") && gn=$(g "$N") && ga=$(g "$A") && printf 'same_commit=%s same_image=%s digests=%s\n' "$( [ -n "$cn" ] && [ "$cn" = "$ca" ] && echo yes || echo no )" "$( [ -n "$gn" ] && [ "$gn" = "$ga" ] && echo yes || echo no )" "$(printf '%s' "$gn" | wc -w | tr -d ' ')"
